children: The FTSE MIB fell 0.2% to 51,987 on Wednesday, amid merger talks in Milan, while concerns over the country’s budget deficit weighed on the index.
Italy’s budget deficit was confirmed at 3.1% in 2025, above the EU’s ceiling, raising concerns over increased spending on defense and energy.
However, Italy plans to confirm a commitment to bring its deficit below 3% this year.
Meanwhile, sovereign yields increased following stronger-than-expected PMI data, raising bets of an ECB rate hike.

Financials were mixed following reports that Italy will abstain from a vote at an MPS (0.4%) shareholder meeting to approve the defensive acquisitions of Generali-controlled (2.3%) Banca Generali and Banco BPM (1.2%).
On the upside, as global oil prices snapped a streak of consecutive declines, energy stocks advanced, led by Eni (2.8%).
Avio rose 1.9% following upbeat revenue estimates from Intesa.

title: FTSE MIB Closes Lower
